Definition: from G2744; a boast (properly, the object; by implication, the act) in a good or a bad sense:--boasting, (whereof) to glory (of), glorying, rejoice(-ing).
BiblicalUsage: Kauchema means the boast itself, the thing you glory in. Romans 4:2 says if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory, but not before God. 1 Corinthians 5:6 warns, your glorying is not good, for a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump. 2 Corinthians 1:14 calls the Corinthians Paul's rejoicing in the day of the Lord Jesus, and Hebrews 3:6 says we are Christ's house, if we hold fast the confidence and the rejoicing of the hope firm unto the end.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the boast tells you what you trust: Abraham had nothing to boast of before God, and neither do I. I hold that the only boast that holds to the end is the hope firm in Christ's house.
